newsitem.title: USA: Rohm stock falls after profit warnings.
newsitem.headline: Rohm stock falls after profit warnings.

text.p: Rohm & Haas Co stock dropped 8-1/2 to 78-3/4 on Wednesday on a warning by the company that it expected first quarter earnings to fall short of the current consensus forecast of $1.70 a share, analysts said.

The stock has fallen from over 90 since a meeting last week with analysts in New York. A company spokeswoman said today that Rohm's chairman told analysts last week that first quarter earnings would not be as good as expectations.

Rohm said on Wednesday that the strength of the dollar meant that it would not reach the first quarter earnings per share consensus forecast of $1.70 but would beat last year's first quarter of $1.46.
Merrill Lynch analyst Frank Mirsch said that the company had met analysts at a Merrill chemical analyst conference last week.
Mirsch said that he had cut Rohm's first quarter earnings estimates by a dime from the consensus figure but maintained their full year at $6.10 per share.
"We believe that the fall in the share price today is way overdone," Mirsch said.
A spokeswoman for Rohm said that some 30 percent of sales were affected by the dollar's strength against European bloc currencies and the Japanese Yen.
"It is a relatively straightforward issue. If you have seen the dollar's strength against European currencies and the yen, it is not going to be positive," said Jeff Spetalnick at Oppenheimer & Co.

Timothy Gerdman specialty chemical analyst at Salomon Brothers said he was recommending investors look for companies which can mask the effects of the currency because they are able to cut internal costs sharply.
"This is a stockpickers market and we are recommending Crompton & Knowles, Valspar and Praxair," he added.
One analyst noted that Rohm's stock had risen sharply in the months up to March 7.
"It is quite thinly traded and there was an inflexion in the stock five days ago," said the analyst.
The stock has come off a 1996 closing high of 94-7/8 on March 7.

One analyst speculated that some of the stock price decline had to do with market talk that the Environmental Protection Agency had issued a recall notice on one of Rohm's products, which the Rohm spokeswoman strongly denied.

"Some months ago, there was a herbicide shipped to farmers which had 25 percent active chemical instead of 24 percent and this was a labelling violation which will result in a fine of $40,000-$50,000, which is immaterial," she said. ((--David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
